# Working with me

My research sits at the intersection of linguistic theory, psycholinguistics and cognitive science. I am particularly interested in working with researchers who want to use precise questions about linguistic representation to investigate cognition, and empirical evidence about processing to refine theories of representation.
</div>

<section class="section">
<div class="section-kicker">Prospective researchers</div>

## DPhil students and postdocs

Projects might concern the cognitive representation of meaning, incremental interpretation, inference and prediction, memory and knowledge, discourse, or related questions at the interface of language and cognition.

A strong fit need not reproduce my existing projects. What matters most is a well-specified question for which linguistic theory and experimental evidence can usefully constrain one another.

Please consult the current Oxford and St Hugh's College pages for formal admissions information and funding arrangements.
</section>

## People and collaborations

The research programme connects with the wider psycholinguistics, semantics and cognitive-science communities at Oxford, including work in the Language and Brain Lab and related groups.

The current roster of students and researchers will be added here once it has been checked against the latest departmental and college listings.
